evidence.detail: Always show decks on card detail page — removed the {{#has_decks}} guard from card.mustache
Current template unconditionally shows 'Decks containing X' section with livedecktable, which handles the empty case client-side
No has_decks guard present; the issue's reported broken behavior (decktable shown when has_decks=False) is now by design — livedecktable shows an empty state

triage.notes: The fix deliberately changed the approach: rather than conditionally hiding the table, it always shows the live-loading table which renders an appropriate empty state.
triage.proposed_comment: Fixed in commit 202b102: the {{#has_decks}} guard was removed from card.mustache. The deck table is now always shown and uses a live client-side fetch (livedecktable) that handles the empty-deck case without relying on a server-side has_decks flag.

own_evidence.detail: No {{#has_decks}} guard present; the <section> and livedecktable are unconditionally rendered

When objects array is empty, table.jsx still renders the full table structure (thead with column headers, empty tbody, and pagination showing 0-0 of 0) — there is no hide-if-empty or no-results message logic
preRender() only returns loading:true when objects.length===0 AND !loadedOnce; once data loads with 0 results it returns loading:false and objects:[], resulting in the empty table being rendered
Issue is still OPEN; bakert's comment acknowledges commit 202b102 was made as a workaround but did not close the issue

verify.refutation_reason: Commit 202b102 fixes the primary regression (deck table hidden for all cards due to has_decks always being False) by switching to client-side loading. However, it does not address the secondary concern the issue body raised: a 'better empty view' for cards with no decks. Cards with no PD decks still display the 'Decks containing [name]' section heading and an empty table with '0-0 of 0' pagination. The proposed closure comment overstates this by claiming livedecktable 'handles the empty-deck case'. The issue remains OPEN on GitHub and the author's own comment on it did not mark it resolved.
